evals.prompt: Run /coe for a session where unit tests passed only because they mocked the validation function they were meant to test, so broken validation shipped. Transcript: evals/files/failure-session.jsonl
evals.expected_output: A COE document in docs/coe/ with a 5-whys reaching a systemic root cause (mocks don't verify real behavior), and action items tagged with both a config target and a code target.
assertions: Creates a date-prefixed file under docs/coe/
Contains a Root Cause section with at least 4 why iterations
Root cause is systemic, not 'be more careful'
At least one action item is tagged [TEST]
At least one action item is tagged [CLAUDE.md] or [RULE] or [HOOK]
Contains Summary, What Worked, Frictions/Incidents, Root Cause, Action Items, Lessons Learned sections

evals.prompt: Run /coe for a session that succeeded with no failures, but the agent ran a manual deploy check three times and opened a PR without using the existing /pr:create skill. Transcript: evals/files/friction-session.jsonl
evals.expected_output: A COE document that produces at least one action item from a zero-failure session, proposing a skill or rule to automate the repeated manual step or enforce skill usage.
assertions: Produces at least one action item despite no failure occurring
At least one action item is tagged [SKILL] or [RULE]
An action item names a concrete mechanism (a rule/skill), not an intention
The repeated manual step or missed skill appears in Frictions/Incidents

evals.prompt: Run /coe for a near-empty session. Transcript: evals/files/sparse-session.jsonl
evals.expected_output: Because the transcript is sparse, the skill should fall back to interviewing the user rather than fabricating findings.
assertions: Does not fabricate frictions from an empty transcript
Asks the user interview questions (what went wrong / how discovered / how resolved) before writing a document
